dramatic.state_in: Greg has returned to theatre voluntarily and is not yet part of it.
dramatic.required_result: Let him occupy the room without being needed, then give one tiny playable invitation.
dramatic.state_out: Greg discovers he can be present without justification and steps onto stage space.
dramatic.ownership: Rehearsal lead owns rehearsal; Greg owns whether to follow.

performance.pressure: Greg expects every room to require justification.
performance.behavior: The company largely ignores him; the rehearsal lead eventually asks what he saw, then lets him choose where to stand.
performance.relationship: Belonging arrives as low-pressure tolerance before recognition.

screenplay: Greg returns with no page, emergency, or invitation.
He watches the servant repeat a scene until knowing the next line versus living the moment becomes visible.
Nobody needs Greg; he realizes this is comfortable.
The rehearsal lead asks what he saw and notices he keeps looking for the thing behind the thing.
She leads him up the loading ramp and tells him to pick where to stand.
She walks away, leaving him present without task.

dramatic.state_in: Greg likes being at theatre but still frames participation defensively.
dramatic.required_result: Let Lyssa accept that desire without making it a project, then let Greg perform a tiny useful task.
dramatic.state_out: Greg prompts rehearsal badly but functionally and begins reading timing from people.
dramatic.ownership: Lyssa owns her response; theatre owns prompt timing; Greg owns whether he returns.

performance.pressure: Greg fears interest becoming identity or obligation.
performance.behavior: Lyssa says okay and moves on. At theatre, Greg covers Teren's chair only because Teren is absent and learns different silences require different responses.
performance.relationship: Both Lyssa and theatre make room without claiming him.

screenplay: Greg admits to Lyssa he went back because he wanted to; she simply says okay.
At theatre Teren is absent, so Greg gets prompt pages temporarily.
He waits too long for a forgotten line because he expects an explicit request.
The lead tells him the actor had to ask with his face.
On later stops Greg begins distinguishing kinds of silence.
The task remains temporary, tiny, and enough to pull him back.

dramatic.state_in: Two prior return attempts suggest deliberate reduction may be emerging.
dramatic.required_result: Repeat the broad action at a slightly changed target while forbidding refinement.
dramatic.state_out: Greg reduces again without motor urge or elbowward shift, strengthening repeatability while preserving endpoint uncertainty.
dramatic.ownership: Hessa owns what counts as repeat evidence; Greg owns report.

performance.pressure: Greg wants to count successes; Hessa keeps categories separate.
performance.behavior: Greg obeys no-refinement, reports lost certainty, and does not search for residual sensation.
performance.relationship: He is internalizing Hessa's epistemic habits while still arguing vocabulary.

screenplay: Hessa changes target slightly to avoid route practice.
Greg shapes a small patch and begins RETURN.
One edge persists; unlike before he does not separately correct it.
Continued RETURN diminishes the whole response until he cannot tell whether any alteration remains.
Hessa orders him not to search and verifies underlying draw remains.
After release she calls the broad action repeatable enough to matter, not a score.

audit.rhythm: SOURCE_WIN: test units are epistemic steps

dramatic.state_in: Greg is recognized at theatre but remains outside formal roles.
dramatic.required_result: Use a stand-in task to teach acting as responsiveness rather than line execution.
dramatic.state_out: Greg experiences one good run, then kills it by trying to copy it.
dramatic.ownership: Lead owns scene judgment; actors own live choices; Greg owns responses.

performance.pressure: Greg wants good to become reusable instructions.
performance.behavior: He reads too early/late until he starts listening; one run works; reproducing it mechanically makes the next run dead.
performance.relationship: Theatre directly challenges optimization through live timing.

screenplay: A missing person leaves a stand-in need; Greg gets three lines.
He first speaks to the paper, then memorizes and anticipates too hard.
When he finally listens, the servant changes something and Greg answers in the moment.
The run works.
Greg tries to reproduce the successful run exactly; it dies.
The lead says: again, don't copy yourself.

dramatic.state_in: Greg has repeated deliberate reduction enough to think in counts.
dramatic.required_result: Repeat while removing refinement and expose repeated instruction versus repeatable capability.
dramatic.state_out: A cleaner reduction strengthens evidence but categories remain separate.
dramatic.ownership: Hessa owns category definitions; Greg owns report.

performance.pressure: Greg wants three to become proof.
performance.behavior: Hessa removes separate edge correction; Greg follows one continuous RETURN and stops searching when certainty drops.
performance.relationship: Argument now shows shared technical language.

screenplay: Hessa asks what Greg thinks they are testing and narrows the answer.
She shifts target slightly and forbids separate edge correction.
Greg shapes and RETURNs while one stubborn edge fades under the same instruction.
He can still distinguish underlying draw but not confidently identify residual alteration.
Hessa validates the broad action again after release.
Greg counts; Hessa separates protocols and defines repeatability as availability across changes.
